info.title: Youjaymharah custom API
info.description:
Endpoints added by this project, on top of the Medusa Store and Admin APIs.

Medusa's own routes (products, carts, orders, customers, returns, ...) are
documented separately and can be downloaded from:

- Store: https://docs.medusajs.com/api/download/store
- Admin: https://docs.medusajs.com/api/download/admin

Every /store route also requires the `x-publishable-api-key` header.
Admin routes marked with `x-required-policies` need those RBAC policies,
which the Store Manager and Marketing roles already hold.

backendUrl.description: Base URL of the Medusa backend.

tags.name: Search
tags.description: Full-text product search over the Search Module's index, with counted facets for refining a results page.

tags.name: Storefront
tags.description: Settings the storefront renders with, edited from Settings › Storefront: home page content (hero, featured collection), sharing & search defaults (title, description, share image, social profiles, indexing, Search Console verification) and product display (New badge days). The public route also includes the brand.

tags.name: Size guides
tags.description: Measurement tables for product pages. A product shows its own guide, else the nearest category's (walking up the category tree), else the store default. Measurements are stored in cm; the storefront converts to inches for display.

tags.name: Product alerts
tags.description: "Notify me" for sold-out sizes and coming-soon products. One email per alert, sent within about 10 minutes of the item becoming buyable, then the alert is done. Asking for an alert is not marketing consent.

tags.name: Marketing
tags.description: A signed-in customer's marketing email preference, backed by the newsletter list and its double opt-in.

tags.name: Branding
tags.description: The store's name, logo and support email, used across customer emails and the storefront.

tags.name: Newsletter
tags.description: Signup, double opt-in confirmation and unsubscribe, plus the admin side: settings, subscribers and the Resend audiences they sync to.

tags.name: Cart reminders
tags.description: Emails reminding shoppers about carts they left (their "shopping bag" on the storefront), at up to three delays after the cart's last change, with links to restore the cart or stop reminders.

tags.name: Accounts
tags.description: Customer accounts beyond Medusa's built-in routes: finishing a social sign-in so one person keeps one customer record.

tags.name: Wishlist
tags.description: Products a shopper has saved. One entry per product, optionally remembering the colour and size they chose. Signed-in customers use /store/customers/me/wishlist; guests use /store/wishlists, where the wishlist ID works like a guest cart's ID, and the guest list is merged into the customer's at sign-in.

tags.name: Returns
tags.description: Customer self-service after purchase: finding a guest order from its number and email, what can still be returned under the store's return policy, and requesting a return. A request becomes a requested return in the admin, without return shipping; staff arrange collection, receive the items and refund.

tags.name: Support
tags.description: Context for customer support in the admin: the emails sent about an order or to a customer and whether they arrived, resending an order confirmation, a customer's saved items, alerts and cart reminders, and looking up payments that didn't become orders.

tags.name: Operations
tags.description: Endpoints for deployment and monitoring rather than shoppers or staff.

tags.name: Scaffolding
tags.description: Placeholder routes left by the Medusa starter. They return 200 with no body and can be deleted.

post.summary: Turn coming soon on or off
post.description: Sets `metadata.coming_soon` without touching other metadata. While on, the product stays published, can't be added to a cart or checked out, and shoppers can ask to be notified. Turning it off emails waiting shoppers on the next alert run once the product has stock. Turning it off on a product that was coming soon is its launch: `metadata.launched_at` is set to now (ISO 8601), which the storefront's "New" badge counts from.

200.description: The new setting, and the launch date if the product has ever been launched from coming soon.

post.summary: Ask to be notified when a product can be bought
post.description: For a sold-out variant (or product) or a coming-soon product. Signed in, the account's email is used and any `email` in the body is ignored; as a guest, `email` is required. Nothing is emailed until the item can be bought. Asking again for the same item returns the waiting alert. `marketing_opt_in` also signs the address up for the newsletter, with its confirmation email; a closed newsletter does not fail the request. Guests always get `alert: null`, so the response does not reveal existing alerts.

get.summary: A listing page's products, filters and counts
get.description: For category, collection, new-arrivals and search pages. `q` narrows the listing to products matching a search term (typo tolerant, within any category or collection given), and `recommended` then means relevance; a first request for a term (no filters, offset 0, default sort) counts towards trending searches. Pass at most one of `category` (a handle; its subcategories' products are included) or `collection` (a handle); neither lists the whole catalogue. Repeat a filter to allow several values (`colour=Black&colour=Navy`): values within a filter are alternatives, filters combine. Each facet counts products against the other filters, so ticking a second value shows what it adds. `fit` lists only short labels from `metadata.fit`. Sorts: `recommended` (buyable first, then newest), `newest`, `price_asc`, `price_desc` (cheapest variant in the region). Results reuse the listing's products for 60 seconds. Rate limited to 240 a minute.

parameters.description: Prices and sorting use this region.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: A search term, up to 128 characters.

get.description: Full-text search over published products in the sales channels the publishable key allows, with counted facets for refining the results. Returns the index' own fields rather than product rows: prices depend on region, currency and any active price list, so fetch /store/products with the returned ids to show them. Repeat a filter parameter to pass several values; values within one filter are OR-ed, and separate filters are AND-ed.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: The text to match, against title, subtitle, description, type, collection and categories. Omit it to browse the facets alone.

post.summary: Receive signed Resend consent, suppression and delivery events
post.description: Requires svix-id, svix-timestamp, and svix-signature computed over the original request bytes. No publishable key or customer session is used. Supports contact.updated opt-outs, permanent email.bounced, email.complained, email.suppressed and suppression.added for consent. email.delivered, email.delivery_delayed, email.bounced, email.complained, email.suppressed and email.failed are also recorded against the sent email for the admin's order and customer pages. Other events are acknowledged without changes. Delivery limit: 64 KiB.

200.description: Acknowledged after workflow handling; duplicates are safe.

400.description: Invalid signature, delivery timestamp or event body.

500.description: Processing failed. Retry the delivery; pending receipts are also recovered by a scheduled job.

post.summary: Find an order from its number and email
post.description: For guests without the link from their confirmation email. Both must match; a miss doesn't say which was wrong. Rate limited to 10 attempts a minute. Load the order itself with GET /store/orders/{id}.

400.description: Missing or invalid publishable API key.

404.description: No order matches that number and email.

get.summary: What can still be returned from an order
get.description: Public like GET /store/orders/{id}: the order ID is the key. Each item's `returnable_quantity` is what has been sent, minus what is already being returned, while its window is open.

400.description: Missing or invalid publishable API key.

post.description: Signed in, the order must be the customer's own. As a guest, `email` must be the order's. Each item must still be returnable in the quantity asked for (see return-options). Reasons come from GET /store/return-reasons. Emails the customer that the request was received. Rate limited to 10 a minute.

400.description: Validation failed; a reason doesn't exist; the email doesn't match or the order isn't the signed-in customer's; or an item can't be returned (window closed, quantity too high, returns off). `message` says which, in words fit to show the customer.

get.description: Pass exactly one of `reference` or `email`. By reference (the one on the customer's Paystack or Credo receipt, or a payment session id): the payment, its cart and order, what the gateway says about it now, and a `verdict` -- `order_placed`, `paid_no_order` (create the order with POST /admin/payment-lookup/create-order), `amount_mismatch` (refund from the gateway's dashboard), `not_paid` or `unknown` (the gateway couldn't be asked). By email: up to 20 recent payment attempts on carts with that email, without asking the gateway.

parameters.name: reference
parameters.description: A payment reference or payment session id.

parameters.name: email
parameters.description: The customer's email, to list their recent attempts.

200.description: The payment and verdict, or the attempts.

400.description: Neither or both of reference and email.

401.description: Missing or invalid admin token or session.

post.summary: Create the order for a paid cart
post.description: For a payment the gateway confirms but that has no order. Asks the gateway again, then completes the cart as the storefront would: payment verified, stock reserved, confirmation emailed. Refused unless the verdict is `paid_no_order`; fails without side effects if an item sold out meanwhile.

400.description: Not a paid cart without an order (the message says why), or the cart can't be completed (e.g. out of stock).

401.description: Missing or invalid admin token or session.

get.description: Newest first, up to 50. One entry per email: retries are folded together. `outcome` comes from Resend's delivery webhooks (email.delivered, email.delivery_delayed, email.bounced, email.complained, email.suppressed, email.failed) and stays null until one arrives. Only emails sent after orders began being recorded on notifications are listed.

401.description: Missing or invalid admin token or session.

post.description: Sends the order confirmation again to the order's current email, as a new email. Each call sends once more, so the dashboard disables the button while a request is in flight.

200.description: Where it was sent. `sent_to` is null when the order has no email, or when `pending` is true: the first attempt failed and the workflow engine is retrying.

401.description: Missing or invalid admin token or session.
